newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Shell's Wavin sees 1996 net up 60 percent.
newsitem.headline: Shell's Wavin sees 1996 net up 60 percent.

text.p: Plastics maker Wavin BV said on Monday it expected 1996 full-year net profit to have risen by more than 60 percent.
In 1995 the company, which is 50 percent owned by Royal Dutch/Shell, posted net profit of 21.1 million guilders on turnover of 1.95 billion.
Turnover for 1996 is seen at about 1.6 billion guilders.

Wavin sold its units producing plastic garbage bags and crates last year to concentrate on its core activity of making plastic pipe systems. The overall effects of this strategy will become visible when full 1996 results are published in April, it said.
Wavin now operates through 34 outlets in 19 European countries and has about 5,000 employees.
The company said its expansion in eastern Europe in the last five years had laid the basis for a considerable turnover growth and an improvement of profitability.
In 1996, Wavin expanded its interests in Poland and Lithuania.
"Wavin will now also seek further expansion outside of Europe," the company said.
